chunks.arabic_text: رِجَالُ الْكَشِّيِّ: حَمْدَوَيْهِ بْنُ نَصِيرٍ، عَنْ يَعْقُوبَ بْنِ يَزِيدَ، عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ، عَنْ جَمِيلَ بْنِ دَرَّاجٍ قَالَ

translations.en: Rijal al-Kashshi: Hamduwayh ibn Nusayr, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj who said:

chunks.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ يَقُولُ: بَشِّرِ الْمُخْبِتِينَ بِالْجَنَّةِ: بَرِيدُ بْنُ مُعَاوِيَةَ الْعَجَلِيُّ، وَأَبُو بَصِيرٍ لَيْثُ بْنُ الْبُخْتَرِيِّ الْمُرَادِيُّ، وَمُحَمَّدُ بْنُ مُسْلِمٍ، وَزُرَارَةُ، أَرْبَعَةٌ نُجَبَاءُ أَمْنَاءُ اللَّهِ عَلَى حَلَالِهِ وَحَرَامِهِ، لَوْلَا هَؤُلَاءِ انْقَطَعَتْ آثَارُ النُّبُوَّةِ وَانْدَرَسَتْ

translations.en: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: Give glad tidings of paradise to the humble: Burayd ibn Muawiya al-Ijli, and Abu Basir Layth ibn al-Bukhtari al-Muradi, and Muhammad ibn Muslim, and Zurara. Four noble-ones, trustees of Allah upon His Halal and Haram. If it were not for these four, the traces of prophethood would have been cut off and erased.

en.summary: This hadith from Al-Kashi highlights the pivotal role of these four 'Nujaba' (distinguished ones) in preserving the transmission of Sharia, emphasizing their status as Allah's trustees over halal and haram. Their collective authority ensured the continuity of prophetic tradition, preventing the loss of religious knowledge during the early Imams' era. This underscores the Shia concept of the infallible Imams relying on a trusted circle of companions to safeguard and disseminate divine law.
en.seo_question: Who are the four noble companions mentioned as trustees of Allah in this hadith?

key_terms.حَلَالِهِ وَحَرَامِهِ: His Halal and Haram (permissible and forbidden)
